title: Pagani Zonda vs Utopia: The Difference Nobody Explains
description:
The Pagani Zonda had a naturally aspirated engine with up to seven point three litres. The Pagani Utopia has a twin-turbocharged engine with less than six. One was made for twenty years, with about one hundred forty cars. The other plans two hundred twenty-nine cars in just a few years. And yet, by our own arithmetic, the newer car is the better one at the thing Pagani cares about most: power for every kilogram. So what really changed in twenty-three years of Pagani? Where did the company keep the same recipe, and where did it throw it away? We went through the published numbers, and the answers surprised us. Starting with the engine, and a detail that most comparisons skip.

Every figure in this video comes from a published source, listed below.
